quest.title: Threadlike Whispers
quest.description: The time you and Tlazolli agreed upon has almost arrived. You prepare to pay her a visit to check on the Blazegem Inscription's progress.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.num: A Prayer for Blessings, Told to Crested Peaks: Act III
chapter.title: Melodious Chant

talks.objective: Go to the Children of Echoes

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What was that noise?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Nechca must have woken up and wants to get out of bed on her own... Sorry, I'll go check on her first.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Nechca! Don't try to get out of bed, just tell Mom if you need anything!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You go ahead and take care of Nechca, Auntie.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #Let's go, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. There are a few things I want to tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: Xilonen! Good thing you're here, I'm wondering if I can—

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The shelf on the left, second row down, first axe on the right... that one's yours. The garden hoe belongs to Iknal and the hammer is Pacal's, so make sure you take the one that's yours.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: I haven't even said why I'm here... But looks like you're about to head out for a break?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yes, but I'm going to take it right here. The temperature's just perfect today.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: Really? But doesn't it feel a lot hotter than usual? I really don't want to stay out in this heat.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Exactly. In hot weather like this, customers don't tend to stick around and talk when they're coming to place orders or pick up the goods.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: I see... Oh, here comes another customer. I'll just leave you to it then, and pick up my axe.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Sure, sounds good to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Xilonen!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we meet again. You two seem to be in good spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: How's your Pilgrim's Chronicle been? Run into any issues?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, everything is fine.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Good. It was also my first time receiving a Pilgrim's Chronicle. Even though I've already turned it over to you...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: There are still a lot of things that could go wrong, so I wasn't sure if there would be any issues.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So, uh... what are the chances that something might still go wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Less than the chances of Mualani accidentally falling off a Spiritway, I'd say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, well that definitely would never happen...

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: I've found the axe, Xilonen. Thanks a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: By the way, Nechca's birthday is coming up real soon. Are you planning to visit her?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I've prepared a gift, and was just getting ready to take it to her.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: *sigh* You're not planning on giving the kid a full set of pliers again, are you? Or lemme guess, woodworking tools?

choices.text: You'd give these kinds of things as... birthday gifts?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That's right. Flowers will wither, toys will break, and snacks are quickly forgotten once they're eaten...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But a set of durable work tools will always stay with you, and get you through many sticky situations.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Still, I won't be giving Nechca any tools this year. She wrote me a letter saying that she'd like a copy of "Tequil the Brave."

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The book is not what you'd call a bestseller, but luckily, I have a few copies in my collection. They were really old editions that were published a long time ago, but they should still be readable...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Haha, children her age love fairy tales. The last time I was at Tlazolli's, I even brought Nechca a—

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Huh? Wait... what did I bring her again? It must have been her favorite thing, but... Uh... Why can't I remember it anymore?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It is quite hot today, seems you're about to pass out from the heat. Do you even remember your own name?

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: My memory can't be this bad. It's just these last few days... *sigh* I've been forgetting things for some odd reason.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: In that case, why don't you use the Blazegem Inscription you have as a memo to engrave some important things to remember?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: After all, that Inscription will never wear out, and it's easy to carry... I'd say that's quite a fitting use for it.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Ahem... You do have a point, but... my Inscription is almost already full.

choices.text: Your name is that long?

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: No, no. I engraved some wishes on my Blazegem Inscription.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: You know, just some dreams that I have for the future and things I'd like to accomplish one day.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Even though Tlazolli has said that from an aesthetic point of view, it would be best for people to keep their Inscriptions short...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: This Blazegem Inscription was still made by a Name Engraver, the forger of Ancient Names themselves.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Everyone thinks that the Inscriptions she made might have some... wondrous powers.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: So, many people who bought Blazegem Inscriptions engraved their wishes and dreams on them in hopes that they would come true.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds kinda like a Wish Granter...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if you do that, won't everyone be able to see your wishes and dreams?

choices.text: I was just wondering the same thing...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Hahaha, don't worry. We usually ask Tlazolli to add the inscriptions for us. She has a unique method of engraving.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: With her method, the light must be at a certain angle in order to see the text.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Without the right angle of lighting, the Blazegem Inscription will just look like a pretty stone.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That's true. In the end, a Blazegem Inscription is essentially just a piece of rock. It doesn't have the power to grant people's wishes.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Making wishes to it is like shouting into an echoing valley — the only one who'll answer is yourself.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But... using it as a journal for your wishes is also fine. Carrying them with you and taking a look from time to time can be a good source of encouragement...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: As long as you don't suddenly change your mind and want to take your wishes back, that is. These things are extremely durable — it would take a lot of effort to change the words.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And I don't think anyone would willingly part with it, either. They're not cheap, and very hard to get. If you ever lost it, you'd just be filled with regret.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Still, it's really strange... given Auntie's skill, how could it take so long for her to make one? I hope someone didn't give her the idea of making fewer and selling for more.

choices.text: Ugh, I know just the person who would do that...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Hahaha! It's true, Cheven could totally have put that in her ear. Still, I don't think it's a bad thing for Tlazolli to make some money by selling these.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: At least she and little Nechca are better off now, and won't have to worry about the cost of treating her illness anymore.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: I was really worried about their family at first, and was even planning to send them some... uh, send some...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Huh? What was I planning to send to Nechca again? Ugh, this memory of mine...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Alright. If you stay out in the heat for any longer, I'm afraid even the Inscription won't be able to save your memory. You should go back and get some rest.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Right... Right. Please give my regards to Tlazolli and Nechca.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: What's going on? Maybe I should go talk to Erinle to get some medicine...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you'll be going to Nechca's birthday party, too, Xilonen? Ooh, perfect, then let's go together!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Sure, but I didn't expect you to know Tlazolli, too. She hasn't even been coming to the tribe much lately, so how did you get a chance to talk with her?

choices.text: Sounds just like one of Cheven's schemes...
Yeah, that could be a little embarrassing...
Did you include all your relatives' names too?
I'd like a set, too! Where can I buy one?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I make these myself, and it's a lot of work. But if you'd like a set, I can make some time and forge one for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! We often camp out in the wild, but a set of Xilonen's tools would make pitching a tent and starting a bonfire a whole lot easier.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain your encounter with Tlazolli to Xilonen...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: So that's how you met her... She even wants to use Volcanic Crystal as a forging material... Guess she's really pulling out all the stops for her daughter.

choices.text: We also wanted to get a gift for Nechca.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Then let's just go and ask. Come on, I want to give her the book anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait a second, aren't birthday gifts supposed to be a surprise?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we ask Nechca, then she'll know what gift we'll be getting her, and that would ruin the surprise!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But if you don't ask her, then how will you know what kind of present she would like?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Here's another idea. Perhaps you can also give her a storybook based on what she wrote in her letter. That might be a good option.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Easy enough, I have loads of those in my bag.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But shouldn't we give it a little more thought? If we all give her books, it might seem like we didn't put much effort into it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xilonen, have you really never asked her what she would like the most? There must be something else she'd like besides books.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Unfortunately, no. Nechca's illness has kept flaring up over the past few years. Apparently, she couldn't do anything during that time other than rest in her bed. She didn't even have the strength to talk to anyone.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It wasn't until recently that she started to recover from her illness and regained the strength to write letters to others.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Anyway, there's no need to overthink it. Worst case scenario, I can split the book into two volumes and we can each give her one.

choices.text: Great idea!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, that's terrible! That would really look like we didn't try!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's just go ask Nechca. Even though it would ruin the surprise, we could at least get her something that would make her happy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, could you tell us a bit more about the book that you're getting her? Is it really that unpopular?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's a little difficult to explain. You see, there are actually two versions of "Tequil the Brave."

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The premise of the book is pretty straightforward. It's basically about a set of twin brothers working to defeat a demon lord.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But after defeating the demon lord, the older brother Tequil discovers that king's spirit has possessed his younger brother, Rimac.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: In the ending of the original story, the older brother kills his younger brother to defeat the demon lord, before himself jumping into a volcano.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I remember there was one line that was super popular at the time. If I still remember right, after being possessed by the Goddess Coatlicue, Rimac said...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: "I do not wish to see your blood be reduced to ash, but I have seen the light of your heart and spirit. Remember my name, brother. As long as you remember me, I will never have left."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So what about the other version of the story?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The other version was released only recently. The author heard a suggestion from someone and suddenly decided to try and make a stake in the fairy tale market, so the story was revised...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: In the revised version, the brothers killed the demon lord together and both survived. According to the author, this gave the story a happy-ever-after kind of ending.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: However, the revised version was not well-received... After a month on the market, it had hardly sold any copies, and the books were collecting dust on the store shelves.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The store owners desperately tried to get rid of the book, and have resorted to all sorts of promotions and discounts to sell it.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Even now, the only edition of Tequil the Brave you can find on the market is the newer one, whereas the older edition is nearly impossible to find.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Anyway, I couldn't bring myself to give such a poorly-rated book to Nechca... So I spent a few days looking, and managed to find a few copies of the old edition in a warehouse.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I picked out a copy that looked relatively new, and wrapped it up as a present for Nechca.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If you're interested, I can give you this extra copy to read. The pages are pretty old, though, so please be gentle with it.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Oh, and here's a copy of the newer edition, too. They gave me a free copy when I went to buy some Xocoatl.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's how they're trying to sell off the book... could it really be that bad? Even Paimon's curious now.

choices.text: That's two more for the collection.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Let's get going. Tlazolli lives pretty far from the tribe, so it'll take us some time to get there.

choices.text: You can read them to me while we're on the road, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, but you'll have to carry Paimon for a while. Once Paimon's done reading it herself, she'll read it out for you.

choices.text: Let's just go and ask Nechca.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, even though it would ruin the surprise, we could at least get her something that would make her happy.

choices.text: But we have no idea what she might like...

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Go on now, Iengu. Nechca is still resting.

dialogues.speaker: Iengu
dialogues.text: *whine*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Tlazolli, we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Oh? What a surprise! And even Xilonen is here, too...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We came to visit Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It's been a while since I've seen you last, Auntie.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I received Nechca's letter. She wanted a copy of Tequil the Brave, right? I've brought the book for her.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: There are several editions of the book in Natlan, and I wasn't sure which version she'd prefer.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I asked a messenger from the Scions of the Canopy. It seems this softcover edition is one of the most popular options, so I bought it for Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Heh, you haven't changed a bit, Xilonen.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Let's go inside. I was just boiling some Xocoatl, so you can all try some.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Xilonen used to love drinking Xocoatl. When she was little, she would always have several cups every time she came to visit me.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: You were already a big girl by the time I finally had my Nechca. Alright, for now, let's—

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Oof...!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Auntie...? Let's go inside.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, please help me get her into the house.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure thing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon will help, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Be good, Iengu, and don't get in the way!

dialogues.speaker: Iengu
dialogues.text: *whine*!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Alright, let's get indoors. Watch your step now, Auntie.

talks.objective: Help Tlazolli into the room to rest

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Sorry, Nechca's illness has been flaring up recently, so I was up for a few nights.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I suddenly started to feel dizzy in the sun... I hope I didn't scare you.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Have a seat. I'll fetch you a few cups of Xocoatl. Please wait a moment...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I've already brought them over. This cup's for you, Aunt Tlazolli. And these are for you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Xocoatl... What does it taste like? Paimon's heard that it can be pretty bitter... {NICKNAME}, could you give it a try first?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Auntie always adds lots of sugar. It won't be bitter.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: The last time you came to visit, you were still just a kid. But now you're a pillar of the Children of Echoes... No, of all Natlan even!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to the drinks I had here, and the books I happened to read.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've been close for quite some time, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard that you two are from the same tribe... but Paimon had no idea you were so close.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: When I was little, my parents were always talking about how skilled Auntie was at forging Ancient Names, and how she was such a good role model for all the rest of us...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The moment I became idle at home, they would toss me into Auntie's workshop to watch and learn...

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Then your parents would go back, I would boil you a pot of Xocoatl, and let you play in the house.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yeah. Then I would drink, and listen to you banging away with your tools in the workshop.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But eventually, she moved out of the tribe to find some more space for her workshop, and I didn't have the chance to visit again after that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why did you seem so familiar with the place when you went to the kitchen for the drinks just now?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Because the layout of this place is identical to her old house.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Let me see... Ah, that should be Nechca's bedroom, then?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: That's right. Hehe, I remember you used to hunker down in the room to read and draw...

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: But you're all grown up now... Even if you wanted to live here, I'm afraid you've already outgrown Nechca's bed.

choices.text: You two seem like family.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: That's how Nechca sees Xilonen, too. Whenever she's feeling better, she always asks me when her penpal sister would be coming to visit.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Well, I'm here now, and even brought a gift as an apology. I'll leave the book here.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: You said Nechca asked you for the book? I hope it wasn't too much trouble to get... Really, I'm surprised that she even asked you for a present. When she's at home, she'd even ask me for permission to eat some snacks.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: *sigh* Maybe I've been too strict with her. She's obviously starting to like her big sister more than her own mother!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Really? Well, I'd say I really haven't done enough to deserve the title of big sister.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I wasn't able to help her when she was sick, and I didn't even come and properly visit her that many times. The only thing I've been able to do is to help her find some books.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Don't be too hard on yourself, Xilonen. You have great responsibilities as the Name Engraver of the tribe. We both know you are far too busy to take care of her.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: The responsibilities on your shoulders also became far heavier when I... gave up on my work.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You just had more important things to tend to, Auntie... No one in the tribe blames you. We all know that Nechca needs her mother's care.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: But that doesn't change the fact that I gave up on my work. And... even now, I still have not found the courage to pick up my hammer again.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I'm sorry to leave you to shoulder all the responsibilities alone, Xilonen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, why so somber all of a sudden... Uh, don't be so sad, everyone! Hasn't Nechca gotten better lately?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Relax, Auntie. I can handle the work. But once Nechca is back on her feet, you should get back to work and let me have a vacation.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You'll be the one who's busy then, and I'll be sitting at the side drinking Xocoatl and cheering you on.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Heh, if that day really comes, you can have as much Xocoatl as you like.

choices.text: So how did Nechca get so sick?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Hehe... If you asked me before, I wouldn't have even been able to talk about it.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: But now that she's gradually recovering... I've also gained some courage to face what happened back then.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Nechca's illness actually originates from the Abyss.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: That night, I was in the tribe, having a discussion over the forging of new Ancient Names.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Before we could finish our discussion, the alarm started to ring outside. A horde of monsters from the Abyss suddenly attacked the tribe, so everyone banded together to fight them off.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I joined the fray as well, and it wasn't until the monsters were repelled that I got back home with some guards from the tribe... But Nechca was gone.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I can't remember how long I spent searching for her... Maybe for two or three days... In the end, we found Nechca at the bottom of a short cliff.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: She was holding a dried-up Embercore Flower in her hand, and there were traces of Abyssal corruption around her wounds.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I know... it was all my fault. Before the incident, Nechca had asked if I could forge an Ancient Name for her.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Work was busy at the time, so I told her that if she could find an Embercore Flower, I would use it as material to forge her an Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Oh Nechca, my daughter... My Nechca... I was holding her in my arms, but no matter how many times I called her name, she wouldn't open her eyes and look at me...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I was the one who decided to move my workshop to the outskirts of our tribe for work... and I was the one who left her home alone.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Oh... *sobs* My daughter, my Nechca... Why do you have to suffer like this? *sobs*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa...! Hey, hey... It's okay, right? Nechca's getting better!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She already has the strength to write letters now, doesn't she? We... Uh well, Xilonen has even brought her a gift!

choices.text: Please drink some water first.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Sorry, I just can't control myself whenever I remember that time.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Phew, alright... it's not every day that we get guests. I really shouldn't be crying like this.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I asked someone to buy some ingredients for me, so why don't you stay for dinner tonight? I'll make some Shrimp Bisque, Grilled Fish in Mint Sauce, and Tower Tacos.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll help! That sounds like a lot to make, and we don't want you to tire yourself out.

choices.text: Let me flex my cooking skills.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Hahaha! Thank you both. But don't worry, it's just a few dishes. I'll be fine.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: You three just need to make sure everything gets eaten up. I can't eat a lot at this age.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, we haven't had anything to eat yet, so don't worry! We'll make sure there are no leftovers!

choices.text: I promise the plates will be picked clean!

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Ah, it just occurred to me that Xilonen likes to eat Cheesy Crab Hotpot. Why don't I make that instead of the Grilled Fish in Mint Sauce? I remember you don't like picking out fish bones.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Both are fine with me. I've learned to just chew up the fish bones now.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Oh, c'mon now. If you don't want to pick out the bones, I can just take them out for you...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Anyway... for dessert, would you like a Cup O' Grainfruit or Chocolate?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cup O' Grainfruit!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Chocolate!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: How about a Cup O' Grainfruit mixed with Chocolate?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Okay, got it. I'll go start cooking, but could you do me a favor in the meantime?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I ordered a bunch of ingredients, and they should be here any minute now. Would you go check by the door and see if they were already here? If so, please bring them in.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: C'mon Xilonen, stop lying around. You shouldn't nap before dinner, it'll ruin your appetite.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hey! I'm not a kid anymore, you know. You don't have to worry about my appetite.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: That's beside the point. If you don't watch out for your health while you're still young, then when you get older, you'll—

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Alright, alright... I'm getting up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll go check on the ingredients with Xilonen. It isn't far, so it shouldn't take us long.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: *sigh* That kid...

choices.text: I can eat an entire fish myself.
Enough talk, let's start with a fried egg!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? She mentioned all those delicious dishes, and you're just going to make a fried egg!?

choices.text: Things will get better.
Is her condition really that serious?
Xilonen seems just like an older sister to Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, no one's come to deliver the ingredients yet... Paimon thought we'd see someone come flying down on a Yumkasaur as soon as we came out.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: A messenger from the Scions of the Canopy wouldn't be flying here. They usually come climbing down the cliffs nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: No need to look, there isn't anyone on the cliffs.

choices.text: So should we keep walking?

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: I—I just saw a ghost! *panting*

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: Hey, you there! Sorry, but does Tlazolli live around here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, are you the one who's supposed to deliver the ingredients?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't see any ingredients...

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: Ingredients? Are you kidding? I was nearly eaten myself!

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: Ugh, never mind that now. Those monsters are still hot on my heels! Please, you've gotta help me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xilonen, we... Huh? Where'd she go?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! She's already gone up to fight the monsters! Let's go help her out!

choices.text: Maybe the delivery person got lost?

dialogues.speaker: Tlapal
dialogues.text: Seriously! Since when have there been so many monsters here?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Alright... That should be it for the monsters. Was easier than I thought.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It also seems we're in luck — the goods weren't damaged either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Strange... we didn't see any monsters on the way here.

choices.text: You must have terrible luck.

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: Yeah right! I use this road to deliver goods all the time, and I've never been attacked like this before.

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: It's the main road in and out of the tribe, so people often come here to clear out any monsters. This area's usually very safe.

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: I don't know what happened, but it seems like all the monsters around here have gone berserk. Even the docile Tepetlisaurs are in a frenzy!

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: *sigh* Tlazolli doesn't even forge Ancient Names anymore, so why can't she just move back to the tribe?

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: If she comes back, Nechca will even be able to find some playmates. She's so young, and hasn't even—

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: Uh... Nechca's playmates... No, wait. I feel like my kids have played with her before. They've even told me about Nechca's favorite game... If I remember right, it was...

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: Strange, I always remembered it before... How could I forget all of a sudden...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look at that! He has a Blazegem Inscription, too.

choices.text: So luck shouldn't be the problem.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You should go back to the tribe — it seems like you had quite the scare today. We'll take the ingredients back for you.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'll carry these bags, you two can carry the rest.

choices.text: Sure thing.

response.speaker: Tlapal
response.text: If you say so! Thank you so much. I guess today's just a really bad day for me to go outside...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's so weird... Why is everyone we've run into today having trouble remembering stuff?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And they're all carrying Blazegem Inscriptions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's not sure how to say it... but she's got a strange feeling about this. Like it's all somehow related...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Once you live long enough, you'll eventually start experiencing strange days like this.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Let's bring the ingredients back. Otherwise, we won't have anything to eat tonight.

choices.text: Paimon can help, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Oh, sure... Uh, Paimon can take care of these Grainfruit that fell out of the bag!

choices.text: Seems there's quite a market for those Inscriptions...
You didn't provoke them, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Ah, you're finally back. What took you so long? I was starting to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: We ran into some small problems, but everything's fine now.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Alright, as long as everything's okay now. You all have a seat, I'll get the food ready. It won't take long.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Tlazolli gets to work on the food. After cooking for some time, delicious dishes are set on the table one after another...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, there's so much tasty food! You're amazing, Tlazolli!

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: They were all pretty simple dishes to make. Don't be shy. Dig in, everyone!

choices.text: What would you like to start with, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon will help herself! Hmm, Paimon will have some of this, and this... oh, and this!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Can I get another serving, please?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—You're done already!? Do you even chew when you're eating!?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Of course. Didn't I say that I chew up the fish bones?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'll have just one more fish, and leave the rest for Nechca.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: It's okay, just go ahead and eat all you'd like. Nechca can't eat these dishes anyway.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Her body is too weak to digest these kinds of things. I'll just make some broth for her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no... But, Paimon thought she had already recovered from her illness.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Injuries caused by the Abyss cannot be undone. The doctor said the fact that she's stable is already quite a miracle.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: But it's okay! Nechca can talk to me now, and can even hold my hand... That's more than I could ask for.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: ...Even if she will never again know that I am her mother.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What do you mean?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: The doctor said the Abyss has had an irreversible effect on Nechca's soul. She... She's lost all her memories from before she was injured.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: The doctor also said that this sort of memory loss isn't like simply forgetting something. Rather, she can no longer remember anything from before that fateful day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But, how does that happen?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: You know about the woven scrolls that the Masters of the Night-Wind use to record things, right?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Well, generally speaking, forgetting things is like when the woven scrolls would gradually start to fade. As long as you re-paint and weave the threads again, the faded memories will come back to life.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: But the case of Nechca's memory loss is as if her woven scroll had been cut in two, and the portion from the past was burned to ashes.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: The books she loved to read, the flowers she took joy to grow... and the time she spent in this house were all cut off by the Abyss, and can never be retrieved again.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: As one example of that, Nechca now only sees me as... a strange, unfamiliar Auntie who claims to be her mother.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: She's a good kid, and doesn't want to upset this lady who's been taking care of her so much, so she still calls me "Mom."

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: But I've always had a feeling that she's constantly wondering about things like... Where is her real mother? Why is she stuck here in this house? Was she abandoned?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Nechca really has no idea that her real mother is right in front of her, and has never left...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: So, you plan on recreating Nechca's woven scroll all by yourself?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Or should I say, you've already started reweaving that scroll long ago?

choices.text: A Blazegem Inscription...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The delivery guy's. I saw it hanging from his waist, so I asked to borrow it from him.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Don't worry. I'll return the Inscription to him once we've figured everything out. These things aren't cheap, after all.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: When did you know?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I noticed it back when Blazegem Inscriptions suddenly became popular among the tribe.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It was then that I also noticed that everyone wearing Blazegem Inscriptions had varying degrees of memory loss.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you've picked up on it too, haven't you?

choices.text: Everyone's memory loss...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: "Accessories made using Ancient Name forging techniques"... For what's only supposed to be a pretty souvenir, this Inscription contains a Phlogiston Engraving with a truly overkill level of complexity.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The shape and patterns of these engravings are also identical to that of an Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: By making just a few slight adjustments to the layout and connections of the main pattern, you can pretty much qualify this Blazegem Inscription as a bona fide Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: ...And yet, you've never told anyone about these engravings in the Blazegem Inscriptions that can be activated at any time.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Am I right, Auntie?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: ...I always knew you were a sharp one, Xilonen.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: That's right. I have a way to cure Nechca and restore all her memories. It's actually quite simple.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I want to forge an Ancient Name for Nechca that contains all of her past memories.

choices.text: You're going to... make an Ancient Name for Nechca?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And the reason they must be approved by the Wayob is because the memories they bear are all stored within the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Extracting those memories from the Ley Lines requires the Wayob's assistance.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But your plan wouldn't need you to do any of that, right, Auntie?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Your Blazegem Inscriptions will help you complete that part of your plan in the Ley Lines' place. You will use the Inscriptions to form a massive memory bank for Nechca.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And the Ancient Name you're trying to forge will be used to extract corresponding memories from the memory bank.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A memory bank? Wait, so the reason all those people were having trouble remembering stuff is because... the Blazegem Inscriptions took away any memories related to Nechca?

choices.text: Even though Nechca has forgotten her own past...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Using other people's memories of Nechca to reconstruct her past... This is the first time I've heard of such an idea.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: You've seen through my plans, Xilonen. You're as outstanding as ever... far more brilliant than me.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I intend to use this method to collate all the memories related to Nechca, and allow her to regain her past again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But, wouldn't extracting memories like that hurt the person carrying the Blazegem Inscription?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Not at all. Every time a Blazegem Inscription extracts memories, the process is under my precise control. That way, there's no chance of anyone in the tribe getting hurt.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: This is the Central Inscription that controls all the other Blazegem Inscriptions...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: ...Which will also soon serve as Nechca's Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You made all this yourself, Tlazolli?

choices.text: Even though it's not an official Ancient Name...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Yes, it was lots and lots of work... it was truly exhausting. Or perhaps... I've just grown old.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: You saw it yourself, I nearly fainted just from being in the sun.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I could collapse tomorrow... or even in the next few moments, but Nechca's Ancient Name is still far from completion.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I've solved the issue of storing memories, but I still don't know how to connect Nechca up to this Central Inscription.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I thought you'd just modify your own Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I considered it, but this matter doesn't have anything to do with my Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: It's of no help to me, and I don't need its help now.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You know the price to pay for making something like this.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Yes, I do. But as long as I can get my Nechca back, I'm willing to do whatever it takes.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Otherwise, Nechca won't have any chance of reclaiming her past once I'm dead and gone.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: She won't remember me, and she won't even remember why her name is Nechca.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: When that time comes, she would be left to drift around the world all alone... unknowing of where she came from, or where she should go.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: She is my daughter, the one to whom I gave the Nechca name... Whether it be as her mother or as a Name Engraver, I can't simply stand by and let her name disappear.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xilonen...

choices.text: Shh, let her think about this for a moment.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'll take this Central Inscription with me.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'm going to completely disassemble it to confirm its components and uses.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I won't make any promises until I've checked everything.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Say goodnight to Nechca for me, Auntie.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: #Oh... wait! I've also finished the Inscriptions for {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Let me fetch them for you.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I'm sorry it took me so long to finish them...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hold on, Auntie.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon have never met Nechca before, so you can't draw any memories from them.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: That wasn't my intention... They're just ordinary gifts. Please, take them...

choices.text: Let her decide what to do.
That's still a lot to do on your own...
Her life was still witnessed by other people...
But Ancient Names must be approved by the Wayob...
Had something to do with Nechca.
Whose is it?
No flying on the table, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Paimon can't reach that dish... Could you give Paimon some? C'mon, c'mon!

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: That kid... She's just like Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Hello again! Back for more tea? I can put on another pot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About "Blazegem Inscriptions"...

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Oh? You'd like to know about their... technical details?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: As you're friends of Xilonen, I'm willing to share that information with you, yes... Let me pick something simple to start with.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: They... Are actually accidental byproducts from my first time forging an Ancient Name.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Then, I accidentally made a mistake with the Phlogiston Engraving of an Ancient Name, creating some kind of "deviation" in the functionality of the Ancient Name.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: It could not guide the "memories" and "emotions" that people feel, but rather it could take certain "memories" within itself.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: At first, I thought it was utterly useless, so I tossed it in with the other defective products. But after Nechca fell ill, I suddenly thought of this "defective" Ancient Name... which is now known as a "Blazegem Inscription."

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: ...Nechca lost her memories of the "past." But that past was clearly real... and there are many witnesses to those events.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I can use that Blazegem Inscription to extract memories related to Nechca from the witnesses.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: And then, by gathering all those memories together, create an entire "memory bank" about Nechca's past for her.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: That way... My little Nechca can come home. She'll remember... that Mama will always be by her side.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About your health...

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I do apologize for making you worry, but... It's just as I said. I could collapse at any moment.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: In order to forge "Ancient Names," I have paid a high price... Or perhaps I should say, I have given everything I can give, even my little Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I'm not bitter towards anyone, nor do I expect anything in return... Right now, all I want is to help Nechca get better.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: And for that, I will offer everything I have and am.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Goodbye. The roads outside are tough going, so please be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: Xilonen! Good thing you're here, I'm wondering if I can—

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The shelf on the left, second row down, first axe on the right... that one's yours. The garden hoe belongs to Iknal and the hammer is Pacal's, so make sure you take the one that's yours.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: I haven't even said why I'm here... But looks like you're about to head out for a break?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yes, but I'm going to take it right here. The temperature's just perfect today.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: Really? But doesn't it feel a lot hotter than usual? I really don't want to stay out in this heat.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Exactly. In hot weather like this, customers don't tend to stick around and talk when they're coming to place orders or pick up the goods.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: I see... Oh, here comes another customer. I'll just leave you to it then, and pick up my ax.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Sure, sounds good to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Xilonen!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we meet again. You two seem to be in good spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: How's your Ancient Name been? Run into any issues?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, everything is fine.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Good. It was my first time working with the Lord of the Night to forge an Ancient Name, and you're not even from Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: There are still a lot of things that could go wrong, so I wasn't sure if there would be any issues.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So, uh... what are the chances that something might still go wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Well, less than the chances of Mualani accidentally falling off a Spiritway, I'd say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, well that definitely would never happen...

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: I've found the ax, Xilonen. Thanks a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: By the way, Nechca's birthday is coming up real soon. Are you planning to visit her?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I've prepared a gift, and was just getting ready to take it to her.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: *sigh* You're not planning on giving the kid a full set of pliers again, are you? Or lemme guess, woodworking tools?

choices.text: You'd give these kinds of things as... birthday gifts?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That's right. Flowers will wither, toys will break, and snacks are quickly forgotten once they're eaten...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But a set of durable work tools will always stay with you, and get you through many sticky situations.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Still, I won't be giving Nechca any tools this year. She wrote me a letter saying that she'd like a copy of "Tequil the Brave."

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The book is not what you'd call a bestseller, but luckily, I have a few copies in my collection. They were really old editions that were published a long time ago, but they should still be readable...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Haha, children her age love fairy tales. The last time I was at Tlazolli's, I even brought Nechca a—

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Huh? Wait... what did I bring her again? It must have been her favorite thing, but... Uh... Why can't I remember it anymore?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It is quite hot today, seems you're about to pass out from the heat. Do you even remember your own name?

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: My memory can't be this bad. It's just these last few days... *sigh* I've been forgetting things for some odd reason.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: In that case, why don't you use the Blazegem Inscription you have as a memo to engrave some important things to remember?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: After all, that Inscription will never wear out, and it's easy to carry... I'd say that's quite a fitting use for it.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Ahem... You do have a point, but... my Inscription is almost already full.

choices.text: Your name is that long?

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: No, no. I engraved some wishes on my Blazegem Inscription.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: You know, just some dreams that I have for the future and things I'd like to accomplish one day.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Even though Tlazolli has said that from an aesthetic point of view, it would be best for people to keep their Inscriptions short...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: This Blazegem Inscription was still made by a Name Engraver, the forger of Ancient Names themselves.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Everyone thinks that the Inscriptions she made might have some... wondrous powers.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: So, many people who bought Blazegem Inscriptions engraved their wishes and dreams on them in hopes that they would come true.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds kinda like a Wish Granter...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if you do that, won't everyone be able to see your wishes and dreams?

choices.text: I was just wondering the same thing...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Hahaha, don't worry. We usually ask Tlazolli to add the inscriptions for us. She has a unique method of engraving.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: With her method, the light must be at a certain angle in order to see the text.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Without the right angle of lighting, the Blazegem Inscription will just look like a pretty stone.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That's true. In the end, a Blazegem Inscription is essentially just a piece of rock. It doesn't have the power to grant people's wishes.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Making wishes to it is like shouting into an echoing valley — the only one who'll answer is yourself.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But... using it as a journal for your wishes is also fine. Carrying them with you and taking a look from time to time can be a good source of encouragement...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: As long as you don't suddenly change your mind and want to take your wishes back, that is. These things are extremely durable — it would take a lot of effort to change the words.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And I don't think anyone would willingly part with it, either. They're not cheap, and very hard to get. If you ever lost it, you'd just be filled with regret.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Still, it's really strange... given Auntie's skill, how could it take so long for her to make one? I hope someone didn't give her the idea of making fewer and selling for more.

choices.text: Ugh, I know just the person who would do that...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Hahaha! It's true, Cheven could totally have put that in her ear. Still, I don't think it's a bad thing for Tlazolli to make some money by selling these.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: At least she and little Nechca are better off now, and won't have to worry about the cost of treating her illness anymore.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: I was really worried about their family at first, and was even planning to send them some... uh, send some...

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Huh? What was I planning to send to Nechca again? Ugh, this memory of mine...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Alright. If you stay out in the heat for any longer, I'm afraid even the Inscription won't be able to save your memory. You should go back and get some rest.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: Right... Right. Please give my regards to Tlazolli and Nechca.

response.speaker: Avilix
response.text: What's going on? Maybe I should go talk to Erinle to get some medicine...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you'll be going to Nechca's birthday party, too, Xilonen? Hehe, perfect, then let's go together!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Sure, but I didn't expect you to know Tlazolli, too. She hasn't even been coming to the tribe much lately, so how did you get a chance to talk with her?

choices.text: Sounds just like one of Cheven's schemes...
Yeah, that could be a little embarrassing...
Did you include all your relatives' names too?
I'd like a set, too! Where can I buy one?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I make these myself, and it's a lot of work. But if you'd like a set, I can make some time and forge one for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! Hehe, we often camp out in the wild, but a set of Xilonen's tools would make pitching a tent and making a bonfire a whole lot easier.
